//: Reviewed classifications for credential write sites, produced by a manual security review and carried forward.
This file ANNOTATES the output of report:credential-writes. It cannot add, remove, hide or reclassify a site.
The reporter prints every site it finds; a site with no entry here prints as "unreviewed", and an entry here
that matches no site prints in the STALE REVIEW NOTES section. Deleting this whole file changes nothing except
that every site prints as "unreviewed".
Keys are file|enclosing-functions|sink|call-shape-digest - never line numbers, never a position among siblings - so
adding a write next to a reviewed one does not detach its note. The digest is credential-write-call-shape.mjs; a "~n"
suffix means two calls in one function share a sink AND a shape, and only those are still told apart by source order.
Run `pnpm report:credential-writes:rekey` when the report prints ORPHANED REVIEW NOTES.
"retired" holds judgement about writes the analysis no longer classifies as a site. It is never joined to anything, so
it can annotate nothing and hide nothing; it exists so a real review is kept instead of deleted, and so it stops being
counted as an orphan. Each entry says why in retiredBecause.
VERDICTS (what the reviewer concluded, not what the tool proved)
cleartext-fallback-unfixed     REAL FINDING. A secret is written in cleartext when safeStorage is unavailable, with no plaintext-policy opt-in. These are the ones to fix.
gated-dev-plaintext-opt-in     Cleartext, but only reachable behind a sanctioned plaintext-policy predicate that refuses in packaged/production builds. The report shows these as gated-by=.
deliberate-plaintext-interop   An external CLI owns the on-disk format and reads it back; Orca cannot encrypt it. Mitigated with 0600 + ownership checks.
locally-minted-handshake-token A random token Orca itself mints for a local handshake; it must be readable at rest for its only purpose.
encrypted-payload              The bytes written are safeStorage ciphertext or a sealed envelope; only the surrounding names matched the vocabulary.
non-secret-payload             Reviewed: the written bytes contain no secret (metadata, pid, diagnostics, screenshot).
orchestrator-forwarding        A call into a routine that writes further down; the write is classified at its own site.
fd-write-not-a-file            An fd-level write whose destination is a pipe, which the sink model cannot distinguish from a file.

src/main/runtime/e2ee-keypair.ts|mintKey.reason: Still writes the mobile transport PRIVATE key with secretKeyFormat: "plaintext" (0600) BY DEFAULT on a host that has neither an OS keychain nor an operator passphrase, which is why this stays classified unfixed. What changed: cleartext is the third choice, not the second. sealIdentitySecret (src/main/runtime/e2ee-identity-envelope.ts) tries the keychain and then an orca-passphrase-v1 envelope (AES-256-GCM under a scrypt-derived operator passphrase, headless, no keyring), and a cleartext identity already on disk is upgraded in place on the first launch that can seal it - no re-pairing. Kept rather than refused because this key is a durable identity: refusing costs no re-auth, it mints a DIFFERENT identity next launch and silently orphans every paired device. Gated on allowsPlaintextE2EEIdentity(), one unmissable operator notice per launch naming the exact file and every fix, and refused outright when ORCA_REQUIRE_SEALED_E2EE_IDENTITY=1. Reads as unguarded here on purpose: the sanctioned registry means dev-only opt-in, which a predicate that must say yes in headless production cannot honour.
